Interface SsComponent

All Superinterfaces:
RSC
All Known Implementing Classes:
DateTimeField, Field, NumberField, SsCheckBox, SsComboBox1, SsComboBox2, SsCurrencyField, SsDateField, SsDbComboBox2, SsFormattedTextField, SsImage, SsIntegerField, SsLabel, SsList1, SsNumericField, SsPercentField, SsSlider, SsSSNField, SsTextArea, SsTextField, SsTimeField, SsTimestampField
public interface SsComponent extends RSC
This Interface presents a RowSet column presented by the visual components in the Seesaw library. It has default methods supporting binding a RowSet column to this component, DBMS access with type conversion, undo/redo, validation, decoration. Most of these default methods bounce to an internal SsCommon class and would be declared final if java supported that. A database column is associated with this component via RowsModel.bind(SsComponent,String). There are only two methods, and the Hook, that need to be implemented by the visual component: cleanField(), getSsComponentHook(). See SsComponent.Hook for a complete example.

The basic components for application use and/or subclassing are found in core components. They are subclassed into a compatibility layer as a replacement for the original SwingSet library.

There are several methods that are typically overridden; they perform customization, receive notification, and do verification: customInit(), checkColumnType(JDBCType), metadataChange(), finishBind(), baseValidate(), componentValidate(), and createDefaultDecorator(). Component developers should be aware of the method isComposite(); override it to return true if the component contains JComponents and some of these descendant components may be focused.

The methods for reading and updating database columns are getColumn*() and setColumn*. With getColumnText(), setColumnText(String) and getColumnObject(Class) values are converted as needed, see ConvertType. For unhandled JDBCTypes, getColumn() and setColumn(Object) are available; see setColumnReader(DbReader) and setColumnUpdater(DbUpdater).

There are methods about column state, status and metadata; like [sg]etAllowNull(), isDirty(), getColumnJDBCType().

There are multiple levels of validation. The validators are executed in the following order, see allValidate(); if there's an error, validation stops, and see SsComponent.ValidationResult.

  1. baseValidate() - method, defaults true
    This checks that the SsComponent's value is more or less correct. For example a mask formatter's valid indicator, JFormattedTextField.isEditValid(); or a SsTextField subclass could check that there's only characters.
  2. componentValidate() - method default true
    A subclass of something that does baseValidate, can use this for more specific validation.
  3. optionally check rowsModel.hasError(SsComponent)
  4. pluginValidate - Application specific validation, per component instance.
    Set at run time with setPluginValidator(Validator). For example check for specific values; or other columns or ... Can apply constraints while editing and avoid errors at commit.

There are Decorators that visually indicate the components state.

When creating an SsComponent, typical usage: 

    class MyComponent extends SomeJComponent implements SsComponent {
        MyComponent() {
            // ...
            // finishSsCommon() MUST BE CALLED AT END OF CONSTRUCTOR
            finishSsCommon();
        }
    }

    • getColumnReader

      default DbSupport.DbReader<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent> getColumnReader()
      Get the columnReader used by getColumn() and internally, when not null, for capturing initial value for undo/redo. This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY. For exampe, see SsImage source code. The columnReader is typically invoked like .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp). The comp is rarely used, and provided for complex situations. The columnReader return the value fetched from the datbase.
      Returns:
      the DbReader used to fetch values from the database

    • setColumnReader

      default void setColumnReader(DbSupport.DbReader<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent> columnReader)
      Set the columnReader used by getColumn() and internally for capturing initial value. This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY. For exampe, see SsImage source code. The columnReader is typically invoked like .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp). The comp is rarely used, and provided just in case. For example with a BLOB or BINARY column 
      setColumnReader((rs, cidx, _) -> { return rs.getBytes(cidx); });
      Parameters:
      columnReader - the DbReader used to fetch values from the database

    • dbChange

      default void dbChange(DbSupport.RunnableSQL r) throws SQLException
      Used when making a change to the database. Typically used by a component listener. It avoids extra RowSet events. See SsComponent.Hook for example usage. May bring up a dialog if there is no row to change, which would usually indicate some kind of internal error.
      Parameters:
      r - code that changes the database
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • setColumnArray

      default boolean setColumnArray(Array columnArray) throws SQLException
      Updates the bound database column with the specified Array.

      Used for List or other component where multiple items can be selected. See SsList1 and DbCollection for low level details on how arrays are read and written. Does not commit the update row.

    • setColumn

      default boolean setColumn(Object value)
      Updates the value of the bound database column; method used by SwingSet component listeners to update the underlying RowSet. Sets the value of the bound database column using the SsComponent's DbSupport.DbUpdater. See getColumnUpdater(). NPE if no columnUpdater. Useful for dealing with JDBCTypes not handled internally. Does not commit the update row.
      Parameters:
      value - to write to the database, may write to the undo/redo stack.
      Returns:
      true if no error

    • getColumnUpdater

      default DbSupport.DbUpdater<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent, Object> getColumnUpdater()
      Get the columnUpdater used by setColumn(Object). This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY. For exampe, see SsImage source code. The columnUpdater is typically invoked like .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp, value). The comp is rarely used, and provided for complex situations.
      Returns:
      the DbUpdater used to update to the database

    • setColumnUpdater

      default void setColumnUpdater(DbSupport.DbUpdater<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent, Object> columnUpdater)
      Set the columnUpdater used by setColumn(Object). This is useful for dealing with ColumnTypes that are are not handled internally, like BLOB and VARBINARY. For exampe, see SsImage source code. The columnUpdater is typically invoked like .apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp, value). The comp is rarely used, and provided just in case. For example with a BLOB or BINARY column: 
      setColumnUpdater((rs, cidx, _, value) -> {
  if (value == null) {
    rs.updateNull(cidx);
    return RowSetOps.UPDATE_NULL;
  } else {
    rs.updateBytes(cidx, (byte[]) value);
    return new RowSetOps.DbUpdate(value);
  }
});
      Parameters:
      columnUpdater - the DbUpdater used to update the database

    • setPluginValidator

      default void setPluginValidator(Validator pluginValidator)
      Install the specified pluginValidator into this component. Each instance can have a unique validator. This is run after all the other validations succeed.
      Parameters:
      pluginValidator - validator to install

    • baseValidate

      default boolean baseValidate()
      Override this to do a low level validation of whether or not the component data is valid. For example, a mask formatter indicates valid; generally simple constraints that are context independent; e.g. month <= 12. There may be additional checks defined by componentValidate() and/or a Validator, see setPluginValidator(Validator); those are checked after baseValidate. The default implementation returns true.
      Returns:
      false for error in data, otherwise true

    • componentValidate

      default boolean componentValidate()
      This has component specific validation, it is called after baseValidate.
      Returns:
      true if successful validation for the type of component

    • allValidate

      default SsComponent.ValidationResult allValidate()
      Run the validators: baseValidate, componentValidate, possibly check RowsModel.hasError(), pluginValidate. The checks are done in order, they stop with any failure.
      Returns:
      result
